bugs.summary: seq_len should get a reverse (?) argument
bugs.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
Unless I'm missing something, there's no safe way to generate the following directly with base functions:

```
rev(seq_len(N))
```

The key being that when `N == 0`, the output is `integer(0)`, imitating the safety of `seq_len()` for that same edge case.

This use case is also quite common (e.g. I'm seeing hundreds of usages like `seq(n, 1)` or `n:1` in a cursory [regex] glance at our nonrandom ~10% subset of CRAN)

The performance cost of the workaround is small but noteworthy in the non-edge case:

```
system.time(rev(seq_len(1e8)))
#    user  system elapsed 
#   0.584   0.798   1.408 
system.time(1e8:1)
#    user  system elapsed 
#       0       0       0 
```

since `1e8:1` uses `ALTREP`.

The first solution that comes to me is a new `reverse` (or some other name) argument to `seq_len()`:

```
seq_len(1e8, reverse = TRUE)
```

As an alternative/in addition, `rev()` should not expand the `ALTREP`.

comments.creator: jaganmn2
comments.text: How about `seq.int(from = n, by = -1L, length.out = n)`?

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
Thanks! That definitely beats the `rev()` option on performance, less so on readability. Especially if `n` is the result of some expensive calculation, we won't want to do

```
seq.int(expensive_n(), by = -1, length.out = expensive_n())
```

so will wind up writing two statements:

```
n <- expensive_n()
seq.int(n, by = -1, length.out = n)
``` 

Which already looks ripe for a wrapper function.

To be fair, in most practical cases, the expensive calculation will produce a data.frame or matrix, which is stored anyway, but code like `seq.int(nrow(x), by = -1, length.out = nrow(x))` is not very appealing either.

Is this down to whether this n↘1 case is important enough to get specific treatment in `base`?

comments.creator: jaganmn2
comments.text:
Note that `seq.int` handles arguments of type `"double"` differently from `seq_len`.  Fractional `from` results in a sequence of type `"double"` rather than `"integer"`, and fractional `length.out` is rounded _up_.

So my suggestion isn't strictly equivalent to `rev(seq_len(n))`.

comments.creator: maechler
comments.text:
So this is about speed mostly, right?

I'm really not an ALTREP expert, but I think a much better solution would be to make  `rev()` ALTREP-aware  which would make the use of  `rev()` 
more generally more attractive.

I think the idiom  `rev(seq(...))`  to be well readable/understandable
and then if you want to be clothe according to latest fashion, you can also use
```
seq(...) |> rev
```

For motivation, I put it in the same boat as `seq_len()`.

Yes, speed, but `1e8:1` _is_ fast already, so robustness is a crucial component too -- speed without sacrificing that one (all-too-common) edge case of `n=0`.
comments.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.text:
FWIW, `seq_len(-n)` is currently an error for positive `n`.  I can imagine arguments for that returning `rev(seq_len(n))` (but with ALTREP) instead.  Then users could do any of `seq_len(n)`, `-seq_len(n)`, `seq_len(-n)` and `-seq_len(-n)` ...

I agree with Martin's comment that it would be nice if `rev` (actually `rev.default`) were aware of ALTREP, and maybe even _sortedness_.

comments.creator: henrikb
comments.text:
> ... I think a much better solution would be to make `rev()` ALTREP-aware which would make the use of `rev()` more generally more attractive.

I agree with this. Currently, in R 4.3.0 and R-devel (2023-05-02 r84376), `rev()` _does expand_ the ALTREP representation of `1:n`, e.g.

```
> x <- seq_len(1e6)
> .Internal(inspect(x))
@564d70ec7cf8 13 INTSXP g0c0 [REF(65535)]  1 : 1000000 (compact)

> rx <- rev(x)
> .Internal(inspect(rx))
@7ff53c83b010 13 INTSXP g0c7 [REF(1)] (len=1000000, tl=0) 1000000,999999,999998,999997,999996,...
```

`rev()` is a generic function and with an integer vector, as here, we end up in S3 method `rev.default()`;

```
> rev.default
function (x) 
if (length(x)) x[length(x):1L] else x
<bytecode: 0x55d5ef37cb90>
<environment: namespace:base>
```

So, to make `rev.default()` ALTREP aware, we would have to implement this in C.  That shouldn't be "too hard" to do.

Another advantage of making `rev.default()` ALP aware would be that it would avoid memory issue with long `1:n` vectors.  Right now, it might fail as in:

```
> x <- seq_len(1e10)
> .Internal(inspect(x))
@55d5f0ba7518 14 REALSXP g0c0 [REF(65535)]  1 : 10000000000 (compact)
> rx <- rev(x)
Error: cannot allocate vector of size 74.5 Gb
```
